The claim for compensation raised in this petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Rajesh Kumar Sharma in a motor accident that took place on 16.02.2017, at about 08:50 am, opposite Majar, Subroto Park, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR Sunita Sharma vs Birbal Ram on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55349793/
1 No.38/17, under Sections 279/304-A IPC was registered at PS Delhi Cantt.

The vehicle involved in this case is a bus bearing registration No. RJ-32PA-2172, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1 (R-1) and owned by respondent no. 2 (R-2).
2.
As per record, the petitioners are wife, mother and children of the deceased.

Succinctly put, facts of case are that on the above said date and time, the deceased was going to his office at Manesar,
Gurugram, Haryana on his motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-6SAL-7663.

When he reached at Dhaula Kaun near Majar, opposite Jhareda Village, the offending vehicle bearing registration No.
RJ-32PA-2172, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in rash and negligent manner, came and hit the motorcycle of deceased due to which he fell down on the road along with his motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the deceased was removed to RR Hospital, Delhi where he was declared brought dead by the doctors.

3. Respondent no. 1 has filed his reply wherein it is stated that he was holding a valid driving license at the time of accident and hence, he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
It is further stated that the alleged offending vehicle was falsely implicated in the present matter.
4. Respondent no. 2 has filed its reply wherein it is stated that they were falsely implicated in the present matter as the accident took place due to sheer negligence on the part of deceased.

5. On 02.08.2017, the following issues were framed by this tribunal:-
1.

Whether Sh. Rajesh Kumar Sharma sustained fatal injuries in accident which occurred on 16.02.2017 at about 08:50 am, opposite Majar, Subroto Park, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. RJ-32PA-2172 driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no.2 ?

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 3.Relief.
6.

The Tribunal has heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Avinash Kumar Lakhanpal, Ld. Counsel for petitioners and Sh. Suresh Bharti, Ld. Counsel for R2 and also perused the entire case record along with written submissions filed on behalf of petitioners.
It is pertinent to mention that R-1 was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 21.09.2022.

7. In support of their claim, petitioners examined four witnesses, PW-1 Sh. Sukanta Bhadra, eye witness of the accident, PW2 Retired SI Om Prakash, Investigating Officer of the case, PW3 Sh. Ram Bilas Yadav, Assistant Commander-II from the office of employer of deceased and PW4 Smt. Sunita,
who is the wife of deceased.
However, in rebuttal, the respondent no. 1 has examined himself as RW1.

One more witness Sh. Lalit Pant from the office of employer of deceased has been examined as Sunita Sharma vs Birbal Ram on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55349793/

The finding on the aforesaid issues is recorded hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs:
1.

Whether Sh. Rajesh Kumar Sharma sustained fatal injuries in accident which occurred on 16.02.2017 at about 08:50 am, opposite Majar, Subroto Park, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. RJ-32PA-2172 driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no.2 ? OPP.
9. Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by vehicle bearing registration No.RJ-32PA-2172.

In order to prove the same, petitioners have examined eye witness Sh. Sukanta Bhadra as PW-1, who deposed that on 16.02.2017 at about 08:30 am to 08:40 pm, one motorcycle Hero Honda and a bus of Rajasthan Roadways at about 20 to 30 feet ahead of him, were moving side by side in left side of the road between AFCAO Gate and Headquarter WAC Gate of Subroto Park and in the meantime, he noticed that there was a collision between said motorcycle and bus side by side.
He further deposed that he called the PCR and ambulance and after 5- 6 minutes, the PCR van arrived at the spot and took away the deceased to the hospital.

He further deposed that he had noted down the registration number of both the vehicles and thereafter, he contacted National Security Guard regarding the accident as there was a sticker of NSG on the motorcycle of deceased.
He further deposed that his statement was recorded by the police as Ex. PW1/1.
He further deposed that the colour of the offending bus was white and there was image of God behind the bus.

10. During cross examination, he deposed that he was coming from his home to his office AFGIS,
AFGIS Bhawan, Subroto Park, New Delhi via Palam Flyover, Army Mall Road, T-point right turn,
Subroto Park, RTR Gate, which is before the RR Hospital gate.
He further deposed that the accident took place at peak time and there was a good volume of traffic at the place of accident.
The offending bus was going from Gurgaon to Dhaula Kaun side.
He further deposed that he had already taken a right turn from the Mall Road, Red light on the above highway and was on his way to Subroto Park when he witnessed the above accident.

11. On the issue of negligence, the petitioners also examined one more witness i.e. the IO Retired SI Om Prakash from MACT cell, Dwarka District, New Delhi as PW2, who had conducted the investigation of subject accident.

He deposed that a person namely Sh. Rajesh Kumar riding on his motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-6SAL-7663, died due to hit caused by the bus of Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation bearing registration No. RJ-32PA-2172.

He further deposed that he had verified all the documents and after completion of investigation, he had filed the DAR before this Tribunal containing all the documents pertaining to the accident as Ex. PW2/1 (colly).

12. In rebuttal, respondent no. 1 also examined himself as RW1 and he tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. RW1/A and relied upon the stand booking report dated 16.02.2017 at 09:51:46 am issued by RSRTC, Dhaula Kaun Stand, New Delhi as Mark A.
He deposed that he was working as driver with RSRTC since 1988.
He used to drive the bus from Delhi to Jaipur and Jaipur to Delhi and plied it on said route approx. 25 times in the year 2017.

He deposed that he had not filed any Sunita Sharma vs Birbal Ram on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55349793/

14. It was held in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, that for the purposes of claim under M.V.Act,
mere filing of the certified copies of the chargesheet of the criminal case for rash and negligent driving is sufficient proof for showing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

"......where the petitioners filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
15.

Reliance has also been placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."

In view of foregoing discussion, it is held that oral evidence led on record by the petitioners on this issue is duly substantiated by the documentary evidence i.e. chargesheet and it stands proved that the aforesaid accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing No. RJ-32PA-2172, which was being driven by respondent No. 1 and owned by respondent No. 2 at the relevant time of accident.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP . 
19.

As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no. 1 has been proved, the petitioners have become entitled to compensation for death of their family member in the said accident but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the heads as discussed hereinafter.
(I) Loss of dependency 20.

The petitioner no.1/wife of deceased has stepped into the witness as PW4 who tendered her evidence by way of her affidavit Ex. PW4/A wherein she deposed that at the time of accident, her deceased husband was working as a Head Constable with National Security Guard on deputation from Border Security Force and earning an income of Rs. 7,17,900/- per annum.

She has tendered on record copy of movement order dated 18.12.2012 as Mark B, copy of office order issued by NSG for appointment of deceased on deputation basis as Mark C, copy of office order dated 11.02.2014 issued by NSG for transferring deceased to Head Officer, NSG as Mark D as well as copy of salary slip of her deceased husband as Mark E. During cross examination, she deposed that the gross salary of deceased as mentioned in the salary slip is Rs. 59,825/- per month, however, after deductions, the net salary of deceased was Rs. 34,482/- per month.

21. In order to prove the same, the petitioners have examined on record Sh. Ram Bilas Yadav,
Assistant Commander-II, National Security Guard, Palam, New Delhi as PW3 who has placed on record attested copies of statement of salary for the months of January, 2017 & February, 2017 as Ex. PW3/A (colly).

He deposed that the deceased Rajesh Kumar was serving at the post of Hawaldar GD(R1) at NSG Headquarter, Mehram Nagar, Palam at the time of accident and the total gross salary of deceased for the month of January, 2017 was Rs. 55,700/-.
22.

Perusal of statement of salary of deceased for the month of January, 2017 as Ex. PW3/A (colly)
reveals that the deceased was working on the post of Head Constable with NSG and was drawing gross salary to the tune of Rs. 55,700/- per month.

In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Sushila Yadav & Ors. ; Iffco Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Chetan Parkash Kaushik & Ors. ; Sushila Yadav & Ors., 2017 LawSuit (Del.) 3185, the allowances in the nature of transport allowance, washing allowance,
metropolitan allowance, ration money and conveyance allowance are regular in nature and are for benefit of the family and hence, these would necessarily result in corresponding savings and thus,
the denial of these allowances would be net loss for the family of deceased.

sentences.text: Hence, these allowances are liable to be included for calculating the salary of deceased.

24. In National Insurance vs. Indra Shrivastava (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court dealt with the issue relating to the connotation of the term 'income' for the purpose of determination of 'just compensation' envisaged in the M.V.Act, 1988 and held as under:
"8.
The term 'income' has different connotations for different purposes.

A court of law, having regard to the change in societal conditions must consider the question not only having regard to pay packet the employee carrier home at the end of the month but also other perks which are beneficial to the members of the entire family.
Loss caused to the family on a death of a near and dear one can hardly be compensated on monetory terms.
xxxxxxxx 17.

The amounts, therefore, which were required to be paid to the deceased by his employer by way of perks, should be included for computation of his monthly income as that would have been added to his monthly income by way of contribution to the family as contradistinguished to the ones which were for his benefit.

We may,
however, hasten to add that from the said amount to income, the statutory amount of tax payable thereupon must be deducted."

25. It is explicit from the testimony of PW3 coupled with the aforesaid exhibited documents that the deceased was working on the post of Head Constable with NSG and was drawing gross salary to the tune of Rs. 55,700/- per month.

Hence, the annual income of deceased comes out to be Rs.
6,68,400/- (Rs. 55,700/- X 12).

26 . In view of the settled law on subject, the tax liability of the deceased, if any, is to be reduced from his above annual earnings as his 'income' means the actual income less the tax paid, as was also approved in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., SLP (Civil) No.
25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017.

"As far as the amounts of pension and gratuity are concerned, these are paid on account of the service rendered by the deceased to his employer.

sentences.text: It is now an established principle of service jurisprudence that pension and gratuity are the property of the deceased.
They are more in the nature of deferred wages.
The deceased employee works throughout his life expecting that on his retirement he will get substantial amount as pension and gratuity.
These amounts are also payable on death, whatever be the cause of death.
Therefore, applying the same principles, the said amount cannot be deducted."
